- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., days 1–5) after price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if recent 5-day average is above 55, forecast tends to be too low; if below 50, forecast tends to be too high — adjust toward recent 5-day mean.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts >0.33 in 2 consecutive days, reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overreaction.
